extraction.body: As the demand for AI products grows, developers are creating and tuning a wider variety of models. While adding new models to our growing catalog on Workers AI, we noticed that not all of them are used equally – leaving infrequently used models occupying valuable GPU space. Efficiency is a core value at Cloudflare, and with GPUs being the scarce commodity they are, we realized that we needed to build something to fully maximize our GPU usage. Omni is an internal platform we’ve built for running and managing AI models on Cloudflare’s edge nodes. It does so by spawning and managing multiple models on a single machine and GPU using lightweight isolation. Omni makes it easy and efficient to run many small and/or low-volume models, combining multiple capabilities by: Cloudflare aims to place GPUs as close as we possibly can to people and applications that are using them. With Omni in place, we’re now able to run more models on every node in our network, improving model availability, minimizing latency, and reducing power consumed by idle GPUs. At a high level, Omni is a platform to run AI models. When an inference request is made on Workers AI, we load the model’s configuration from Workers KV and our routing layer forwards it to the closest Omni instance that has available capacity. For inferences using the Asynchronous Batch API , we route to an Omni instance that is idle, which is typically in a location where it’s night. Omni runs a few checks on the inference request, runs model specific pre and post processing, then hands the request over to the model. If you’re developing an AI application, a typical setup is having a container or a VM dedicated to running a single model with a GPU attached to it. This is simple. But it’s also heavy-handed — because it requires managing the entire stack from provisioning the VM, installing GPU drivers, downloading model weights, and managing the Python environment. At scale, managing infrastructure this way is incredibly time consuming and often requires an entire team. If you’re using Workers AI, we handle all of this for you. Omni uses a single control plane for running multiple models, called the scheduler, which automatically provisions models and spawns new instances as your traffic scales. When starting a new model instance, it downloads model weights, Python code, and any other dependencies. Omni’s scheduler provides fine-grained control and visibility over the model’s lifecycle: it receives incoming inference requests and routes them to the corresponding model processes, being sure to distribute the load between multiple GPUs. It then makes sure the model processes are running, rolls out new versions as they are released, and restarts itself when detecting errors or failure states. It also collects metrics for billing and emits logs. The inference itself is done by a per-model process, supervised by the scheduler. It receives the inference request and some metadata, then sends back a response. Depending on the model, the response can be various types; for instance, a JSON object or a SSE stream for text generation, or binary for image generation. The scheduler and the child processes communicate by passing messages over Inter-Process Communication (IPC). Usually the inference request is buffered in the scheduler for applying features, like prompt templating or tool calling, before the request is passed to the child process. For potentially large binary requests, the scheduler hands over the underlying TCP connection to the child process for consuming the request body directly. Typically, deploying a model requires its own dedicated container, but we want to colocate more models on a single container to conserve memory and GPU capacity. In order to do so, we needed finer-grained controls over CPU memory and the ability to isolate a model from its dependencies and environment. We deploy Omni in two configurations; a container running multiple models or bare metal running a single model. In both cases, process isolation and Python virtual environments allow us to isolate models with different dependencies by creating namespaces and are limited by cgroups . Python doesn’t take into account cgroups memory limits for memory allocations, which can lead to OOM errors. Many AI Python libraries rely on psutil for pre-allocating CPU memory. psutil reads /proc/meminfo to determine how much memory is available. Since in Omni each model has its own configurable memory limits, we need psutil to reflect the current usage and limits for a given model, not for the entire system. The solution for us was to create a virtual file system, using fuse , to mount our own version of /proc/meminfo which reflects the model’s current usage and limits. To illustrate this, here’s an Omni instance running a model (running as pid 8). If we enter the mount namespace and look at /proc/meminfo it will reflect the model’s configuration: In this case the model has 7Gib of memory available and the entire container 15Gib. If the model tries to allocate more than 7Gib of memory, it will be OOM killed and restarted by the scheduler’s process manager, without causing any problems to the other models. For isolating Python and some system dependencies, each model runs in a Python virtual environment, managed by uv . Dependencies are cached on the machine and, if possible, shared between models (uv uses symbolic links between its cache and virtual environments). Also separated processes for models allows to have different CUDA contexts and isolation for error recovery. Some models don’t receive enough traffic to fully utilize a GPU, and with Omni we can pack more models on a single GPU, freeing up capacity for other workloads. When it comes to GPU memory management, Omni has two main jobs: safely over-commit GPU memory, so that more models than normal can share a single GPU, and enforce memory limits, to prevent any single model from running out of memory while running. Over-committing memory means allocating more memory than is physically available to the device. For example, if a GPU has 10 Gib of memory, Omni would allow 2 models of 10Gib each on that GPU. Right now, Omni is configured to run 13 models and is allocating about 400% GPU memory on a single GPU, saving up 4 GPUs. Omni does this by injecting a CUDA stub library that intercepts CUDA memory allocations (cuMalloc* or cudaMalloc*) calls and forces memory allocations to be performed in unified memory mode . In Unified memory mode CUDA shares the same memory address space for both the GPU and the CPU: In practice this is what memory over-commitment looks like: imagine 3 models (A, B and C). Models A+B fit in the GPU’s memory but C takes up the entire memory. The trade-off is added latency: if performing an inference requires memory that is currently on the host system, it must be transferred to the GPU. For smaller models, this latency is minimal, because with PCIe 4.0, the physical bus between your GPU and system, provides 32 GB/sec of bandwidth. On the other hand, if a model need to be “cold started” i.e. it’s been swapped out because it hasn’t been used in a while, the system may need to swap back the entire model – a larger sized model, for example, might use 5Gib of GPU memory for weights and caches, and would take ~156ms to be swapped back into the GPU. Naturally, over time, inactive models are put into CPU memory, while active models stay hot in the GPU. Rather than allowing the model to choose how much GPU memory it uses, AI frameworks tend to pre-allocate as much GPU memory as possible for performance reasons, making co-locating models more complicated. Omni allows us to control how much memory is actually exposed to any given model to prevent a greedy model from over-using the GPU allocated to it. We do this by overriding the CUDA runtime and driver APIs ( cudaMemGetInfo and cuMemGetInfo ). Instead of exposing the entire GPU memory, we only expose a subset of memory to each model. AI models can run in a variety of inference engines or backends: vLLM , Python, and now our very own inference engine, Infire . While models have different capabilities, each model needs to support Workers AI features , like batching and function calling. Omni acts as a unified layer for integrating these systems. It integrates into our internal routing and scheduling systems, and provides a Python API for our engineering team to add new models more easily. Let’s take a closer look at how Omni does this in practice: Similar to how a JavaScript Worker works, Omni calls a request handler, running the model’s logic and returning a response. Omni installs Python dependencies at model startup. We run an internal Python registry and mirror the public registry. In either case we declare dependencies in requirements.txt: The handle_request function can be async and return different Python types, including pydantic objects. Omni will convert the return value into a Workers AI response for the eyeball. A Python package is injected, named omni, containing all the Python APIs to interact with the request, the Workers AI systems, building Responses, error handling, etc. Internally we publish it as regular Python package to be used in standalone, for unit testing for instance: Omni allows us to run models more efficiently by spawning them from a single control plane and implementing lightweight process isolation. This enables quick starting and stopping of models, isolated file systems for managing Python and system dependencies, and over-committing GPU memory to run more models on a single GPU. This improves the performance for our entire Workers AI stack, reduces the cost of running GPUs, and allows us to ship new models and features quickly and safely. Right now, Omni is running in production on a handful of models in the Workers AI catalog, and we’re adding more every week. Check out Workers AI today to experience Omni’s performance benefits on your AI application.

sources.title: Nvidia backs Indian startup helping companies run AI models with fewer GPUs
passages: As the AI boom strains computing capacity, Nvidia has backed Indian startup Simplismart in a $14 million funding round, betting on software that helps companies run AI models more efficiently and, in some cases, with fewer GPUs.
Jain, however, argued that making AI inference more efficient could ultimately benefit Nvidia by making its hardware more attractive to customers and encouraging wider adoption of AI applications.
Simplismart says it helped AI video-generation platform InVideo cut its GPU serving costs by 56% using its software.
The startup also works with AI video companies HeyGen and Higgsfield, as well as enterprise AI startup Ema, among others.
Moreover, Indian cloud provider Yotta uses Simplismart’s technology to power the serverless AI inference service within its Shakti Studio platform.
Alongside its investment, Nvidia has been working with Simplismart on technical integrations, including around its Dynamo inference software, Jain told TechCrunch.

A growing number of startups are also developing tools to make AI models faster and cheaper to run as there is growing demand in this segment, driven by rising demand for AI applications and the need to make better use of expensive GPU resources.
Nvidia participated in the all-primary Series B round alongside Accel, Shastra VC, and Micromax, with Dallas Venture Capital leading the investment.
The deal values the four-year-old startup at about $100 million, including the new funding.
Companies are nowadays spending heavily on GPUs to power AI applications, but running those models reliably and economically at scale remains a challenge.
Different workloads demand distinct trade-offs between speed, cost, and performance.
Deploying and operating AI models to meet business requirements often also requires complex adjustments.

He added that companies instead need to run AI models at speeds and costs that make sense for their specific applications. It says it can optimize factors such as how quickly a model responds, how many requests it handles, and how much computing power it consumes, helping companies get more out of their existing GPU stack. The startup also works with AI video companies HeyGen and Higgsfield, as well as enterprise AI startup Ema, among others. Moreover, Indian cloud provider Yotta uses Simplismart’s technology to power the serverless AI inference service within its Shakti Studio platform. extraction.body: As the demand for AI products grows, developers are creating and tuning a wider variety of models. While adding new models to our growing catalog on Workers AI, we noticed that not all of them are used equally – leaving infrequently used models occupying valuable GPU space. Efficiency is a core value at Cloudflare, and with GPUs being the scarce commodity they are, we realized that we needed to build something to fully maximize our GPU usage. Omni is an internal platform we’ve built for running and managing AI models on Cloudflare’s edge nodes. It does so by spawning and managing multiple models on a single machine and GPU using lightweight isolation. Omni makes it easy and efficient to run many small and/or low-volume models, combining multiple capabilities by: Cloudflare aims to place GPUs as close as we possibly can to people and applications that are using them. With Omni in place, we’re now able to run more models on every node in our network, improving model availability, minimizing latency, and reducing power consumed by idle GPUs. At a high level, Omni is a platform to run AI models. When an inference request is made on Workers AI, we load the model’s configuration from Workers KV and our routing layer forwards it to the closest Omni instance that has available capacity. For inferences using the Asynchronous Batch API , we route to an Omni instance that is idle, which is typically in a location where it’s night. Omni runs a few checks on the inference request, runs model specific pre and post processing, then hands the request over to the model. If you’re developing an AI application, a typical setup is having a container or a VM dedicated to running a single model with a GPU attached to it. This is simple. But it’s also heavy-handed — because it requires managing the entire stack from provisioning the VM, installing GPU drivers, downloading model weights, and managing the Python environment. At scale, managing infrastructure this way is incredibly time consuming and often requires an entire team. If you’re using Workers AI, we handle all of this for you. Omni uses a single control plane for running multiple models, called the scheduler, which automatically provisions models and spawns new instances as your traffic scales. When starting a new model instance, it downloads model weights, Python code, and any other dependencies. Omni’s scheduler provides fine-grained control and visibility over the model’s lifecycle: it receives incoming inference requests and routes them to the corresponding model processes, being sure to distribute the load between multiple GPUs. It then makes sure the model processes are running, rolls out new versions as they are released, and restarts itself when detecting errors or failure states. It also collects metrics for billing and emits logs. The inference itself is done by a per-model process, supervised by the scheduler. It receives the inference request and some metadata, then sends back a response. Depending on the model, the response can be various types; for instance, a JSON object or a SSE stream for text generation, or binary for image generation. The scheduler and the child processes communicate by passing messages over Inter-Process Communication (IPC). Usually the inference request is buffered in the scheduler for applying features, like prompt templating or tool calling, before the request is passed to the child process. For potentially large binary requests, the scheduler hands over the underlying TCP connection to the child process for consuming the request body directly. Typically, deploying a model requires its own dedicated container, but we want to colocate more models on a single container to conserve memory and GPU capacity. In order to do so, we needed finer-grained controls over CPU memory and the ability to isolate a model from its dependencies and environment. We deploy Omni in two configurations; a container running multiple models or bare metal running a single model. In both cases, process isolation and Python virtual environments allow us to isolate models with different dependencies by creating namespaces and are limited by cgroups . Python doesn’t take into account cgroups memory limits for memory allocations, which can lead to OOM errors. Many AI Python libraries rely on psutil for pre-allocating CPU memory. psutil reads /proc/meminfo to determine how much memory is available. Since in Omni each model has its own configurable memory limits, we need psutil to reflect the current usage and limits for a given model, not for the entire system. The solution for us was to create a virtual file system, using fuse , to mount our own version of /proc/meminfo which reflects the model’s current usage and limits. To illustrate this, here’s an Omni instance running a model (running as pid 8). If we enter the mount namespace and look at /proc/meminfo it will reflect the model’s configuration: In this case the model has 7Gib of memory available and the entire container 15Gib. If the model tries to allocate more than 7Gib of memory, it will be OOM killed and restarted by the scheduler’s process manager, without causing any problems to the other models. For isolating Python and some system dependencies, each model runs in a Python virtual environment, managed by uv . Dependencies are cached on the machine and, if possible, shared between models (uv uses symbolic links between its cache and virtual environments). Also separated processes for models allows to have different CUDA contexts and isolation for error recovery. Some models don’t receive enough traffic to fully utilize a GPU, and with Omni we can pack more models on a single GPU, freeing up capacity for other workloads. When it comes to GPU memory management, Omni has two main jobs: safely over-commit GPU memory, so that more models than normal can share a single GPU, and enforce memory limits, to prevent any single model from running out of memory while running. Over-committing memory means allocating more memory than is physically available to the device. For example, if a GPU has 10 Gib of memory, Omni would allow 2 models of 10Gib each on that GPU. Right now, Omni is configured to run 13 models and is allocating about 400% GPU memory on a single GPU, saving up 4 GPUs. Omni does this by injecting a CUDA stub library that intercepts CUDA memory allocations (cuMalloc* or cudaMalloc*) calls and forces memory allocations to be performed in unified memory mode . In Unified memory mode CUDA shares the same memory address space for both the GPU and the CPU: In practice this is what memory over-commitment looks like: imagine 3 models (A, B and C). Models A+B fit in the GPU’s memory but C takes up the entire memory. The trade-off is added latency: if performing an inference requires memory that is currently on the host system, it must be transferred to the GPU. For smaller models, this latency is minimal, because with PCIe 4.0, the physical bus between your GPU and system, provides 32 GB/sec of bandwidth. On the other hand, if a model need to be “cold started” i.e. it’s been swapped out because it hasn’t been used in a while, the system may need to swap back the entire model – a larger sized model, for example, might use 5Gib of GPU memory for weights and caches, and would take ~156ms to be swapped back into the GPU. Naturally, over time, inactive models are put into CPU memory, while active models stay hot in the GPU. Rather than allowing the model to choose how much GPU memory it uses, AI frameworks tend to pre-allocate as much GPU memory as possible for performance reasons, making co-locating models more complicated. Omni allows us to control how much memory is actually exposed to any given model to prevent a greedy model from over-using the GPU allocated to it. We do this by overriding the CUDA runtime and driver APIs ( cudaMemGetInfo and cuMemGetInfo ). Instead of exposing the entire GPU memory, we only expose a subset of memory to each model. AI models can run in a variety of inference engines or backends: vLLM , Python, and now our very own inference engine, Infire . While models have different capabilities, each model needs to support Workers AI features , like batching and function calling. Omni acts as a unified layer for integrating these systems. It integrates into our internal routing and scheduling systems, and provides a Python API for our engineering team to add new models more easily. Let’s take a closer look at how Omni does this in practice: Similar to how a JavaScript Worker works, Omni calls a request handler, running the model’s logic and returning a response. Omni installs Python dependencies at model startup. We run an internal Python registry and mirror the public registry. In either case we declare dependencies in requirements.txt: The handle_request function can be async and return different Python types, including pydantic objects. Omni will convert the return value into a Workers AI response for the eyeball. A Python package is injected, named omni, containing all the Python APIs to interact with the request, the Workers AI systems, building Responses, error handling, etc. Internally we publish it as regular Python package to be used in standalone, for unit testing for instance: Omni allows us to run models more efficiently by spawning them from a single control plane and implementing lightweight process isolation. This enables quick starting and stopping of models, isolated file systems for managing Python and system dependencies, and over-committing GPU memory to run more models on a single GPU. This improves the performance for our entire Workers AI stack, reduces the cost of running GPUs, and allows us to ship new models and features quickly and safely. Right now, Omni is running in production on a handful of models in the Workers AI catalog, and we’re adding more every week. Check out Workers AI today to experience Omni’s performance benefits on your AI application.

extraction.body: As the AI boom strains computing capacity, Nvidia has backed Indian startup Simplismart in a $14 million funding round, betting on software that helps companies run AI models more efficiently and, in some cases, with fewer GPUs. Nvidia participated in the all-primary Series B round alongside Accel, Shastra VC, and Micromax, with Dallas Venture Capital leading the investment. The deal values the four-year-old startup at about $100 million, including the new funding. Companies are nowadays spending heavily on GPUs to power AI applications, but running those models reliably and economically at scale remains a challenge. Different workloads demand distinct trade-offs between speed, cost, and performance. Deploying and operating AI models to meet business requirements often also requires complex adjustments. Simplismart says its software automates much of that work, tailoring how models run on existing computing infrastructure instead of requiring customers to manage those configurations themselves. “Nobody actually needs the fastest or the cheapest inference,” Amritanshu Jain (pictured above, left), co-founder and CEO of Simplismart, said in an interview. He added that companies instead need to run AI models at speeds and costs that make sense for their specific applications. Simplismart’s software sits between AI models and the computing infrastructure they run on and adjusts how models are deployed and managed to meet customers’ requirements. It says it can optimize factors such as how quickly a model responds, how many requests it handles, and how much computing power it consumes, helping companies get more out of their existing GPU stack. The Bengaluru-based startup offers companies a way to deploy and run AI models through its own platform or within their existing cloud and on-premises infrastructure. It also provides tools to fine-tune models, automatically scale computing resources as demand changes, and monitor performance. Additionally, Simplismart allows cloud providers build and operate their own AI inference services on GPU infrastructure using its software. Simplismart says it helped AI video-generation platform InVideo cut its GPU serving costs by 56% using its software. The startup also works with AI video companies HeyGen and Higgsfield, as well as enterprise AI startup Ema, among others. Moreover, Indian cloud provider Yotta uses Simplismart’s technology to power the serverless AI inference service within its Shakti Studio platform. Simplismart’s annualized revenue run rate has grown 14-fold over the past six months to an eight-figure sum, Jain told TechCrunch. The figure is based on recent customer usage rather than contracted recurring revenue and excludes revenue passed through to infrastructure providers, the company said. He did not disclose the exact figure. More than half of Simplismart’s revenue comes from the U.S., despite the startup having more customers in India, Jain said. Alongside its investment, Nvidia has been working with Simplismart on technical integrations, including around its Dynamo inference software, Jain told TechCrunch. The collaboration involves Simplismart’s engineers and Nvidia’s solutions architects, while Nvidia has also helped introduce the startup to potential customers and partners, Jain stated. Interestingly, the investment presents an apparent paradox as Nvidia, the dominant supplier of AI chips, is backing software that can help companies run some workloads with fewer GPUs. Jain, however, argued that making AI inference more efficient could ultimately benefit Nvidia by making its hardware more attractive to customers and encouraging wider adoption of AI applications. Simplismart is serving customers in an increasingly crowded market for AI inference software, competing with offerings from Nvidia itself, as well as major cloud providers and hyperscalers including Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure. A growing number of startups are also developing tools to make AI models faster and cheaper to run as there is growing demand in this segment, driven by rising demand for AI applications and the need to make better use of expensive GPU resources. “Where we tend to win is where people have to be more stringent on their SLAs [service-level agreements] and TCO [total cost of ownership],” Jain said, referring to demanding performance requirements and tight cost constraints. Unlike rivals that offer preset options for faster or cheaper inference, Simplismart aims to find a balance tailored to each customer’s needs, he said. Founded in 2022 by former Oracle engineer Jain and former Google engineer Devansh Ghatak (pictured above, right), Simplismart grew out of the pair’s experience building and deploying machine-learning systems. The two met while studying at BITS Pilani, and the startup now employs 58 people, Jain said. Simplismart plans to use the new funding to expand its presence in the U.S., grow its team, and invest further in developing its inference software. Jain told TechCrunch that the U.S. remains a key market for the startup as it looks to build on its existing customer base there. The funding announcement follows a report by Indian English daily The Economic Times that Simplismart was in talks to raise $40 million to $50 million at a valuation of $300 million to $400 million. Asked about the report, Jain declined to comment, saying the startup was not actively fundraising. He added that the Series B was closed and would not be extended. Additionally, Simplismart allows cloud providers build and operate their own AI inference services on GPU infrastructure using its software.

Simplismart says it helped AI video-generation platform InVideo cut its GPU serving costs by 56% using its software. The startup also works with AI video companies HeyGen and Higgsfield, as well as enterprise AI startup Ema, among others. Moreover, Indian cloud provider Yotta uses Simplismart’s technology to power the serverless AI inference service within its Shakti Studio platform.

Simplismart’s annualized revenue run rate has grown 14-fold over the past six months to an eight-figure sum, Jain told TechCrunch. The figure is based on recent customer usage rather than contracted recurring revenue and excludes revenue passed through to infrastructure providers, the company said. He did not disclose the exact figure.
More than half of Simplismart’s revenue comes from the U.S., despite the startup having more customers in India, Jain said.

Alongside its investment, Nvidia has been working with Simplismart on technical integrations, including around its Dynamo inference software, Jain told TechCrunch. The collaboration involves Simplismart’s engineers and Nvidia’s solutions architects, while Nvidia has also helped introduce the startup to potential customers and partners, Jain stated.

Interestingly, the investment presents an apparent paradox as Nvidia, the dominant supplier of AI chips, is backing software that can help companies run some workloads with fewer GPUs. Jain, however, argued that making AI inference more efficient could ultimately benefit Nvidia by making its hardware more attractive to customers and encouraging wider adoption of AI applications.

Simplismart is serving customers in an increasingly crowded market for AI inference software, competing with offerings from Nvidia itself, as well as major cloud providers and hyperscalers including Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure. A growing number of startups are also developing tools to make AI models faster and cheaper to run as there is growing demand in this segment, driven by rising demand for AI applications and the need to make better use of expensive GPU resources.

“Where we tend to win is where people have to be more stringent on their SLAs [service-level agreements] and TCO [total cost of ownership],” Jain said, referring to demanding performance requirements and tight cost constraints. Unlike rivals that offer preset options for faster or cheaper inference, Simplismart aims to find a balance tailored to each customer’s needs, he said.

Founded in 2022 by former Oracle engineer Jain and former Google engineer Devansh Ghatak (pictured above, right), Simplismart grew out of the pair’s experience building and deploying machine-learning systems. The two met while studying at BITS Pilani, and the startup now employs 58 people, Jain said.

Simplismart plans to use the new funding to expand its presence in the U.S., grow its team, and invest further in developing its inference software. Jain told TechCrunch that the U.S. remains a key market for the startup as it looks to build on its existing customer base there.

The funding announcement follows a report by Indian English daily The Economic Times that Simplismart was in talks to raise $40 million to $50 million at a valuation of $300 million to $400 million. Asked about the report, Jain declined to comment, saying the startup was not actively fundraising. He added that the Series B was closed and would not be extended.

extraction.body: Apple has just released iOS 27.2, bringing Apple Pencil support to the iPhone Duo. The software update also includes an “Edge Light” feature for the iPhone Duo that’s intended to illuminate your face during video calls. Apple previously said the iPhone Duo would add support for the Apple Pencil “later this year.” The company’s first foldable comes with revamped iOS 27 controls designed to work across the device’s 7.6-inch inner display and 5.4-inch outer screen. Many major apps, like Netflix, Prime Video, and Microsoft Outlook, already support the Duo’s extra screen real estate, but some still need some work. The iOS 27.2 update also allows Siri AI to take suggested actions in Messages, while adding support for Siri AI in more languages, including French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish. Apple is rolling out support for Google’s SynthID AI watermark in Photos and Image Playground, too, according to 9to5Mac. Other smaller but notable updates include user profiles on the Apple TV app on iPhone. The Apple Podcasts app is also replacing its “Up Next” queue with a list of “New Episodes,” along with a “Continue Playing” section just beneath it. And group calls on FaceTime now support dual capture so you can show both what’s visible from your selfie cam and your back cameras. Apple also released macOS 27.2 Golden Gate, watchOS 27.2, visionOS 27.2, tvOS 27.2, and HomePod 27.2.

The update adds Apple Pencil support and Edge Light, a handy feature that improves visibility during video calls in low-light conditions. The iPhone Duo now supports the Apple Pencil (USB-C) on both its inner and outer displays. However, support is limited to the USB-C model. The Apple Pencil Pro and other Pencil models are not compatible with the foldable at the moment. The addition makes the iPhone Duo more versatile, especially for users who want to use its large inner display for note-taking and productivity. Moreover, there's Edge Light now, a feature previously available on macOS. For those unaware, it illuminates the user's face by displaying light around the edges of the screen, helping them look clearer during video calls in dimly lit environments. Edge Light works with FaceTime and third-party apps such as Zoom, eliminating the need for a separate light source in many situations. It should also pair well with the iPhone Duo's foldable design, which allows users to prop up the phone for hands-free calls. Beyond these iPhone Duo-exclusive additions, iOS 27.2 introduces several other improvements for eligible Apple iPhones. For starters, Siri AI gets support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish, alongside better use of personal context and previous conversations on Apple Intelligence supported devices. The update also brings suggested actions to Messages, user profiles to Apple TV, a refreshed Podcasts layout and expanded Dual Capture support for group FaceTime calls. To install the update, head over to Settings -> General -> Software Update on your eligible iPhone.

Many major apps, like Netflix, Prime Video, and Microsoft Outlook, already support the Duo’s extra screen real estate, but some still need some work. Other smaller but notable updates include user profiles on the Apple TV app on iPhone. The Apple Podcasts app is also replacing its “Up Next” queue with a list of “New Episodes,” along with a “Continue Playing” section just beneath it. And group calls on FaceTime now support dual capture so you can show both what’s visible from your selfie cam and your back cameras. Apple also released macOS 27.2 Golden Gate, watchOS 27.2, visionOS 27.2, tvOS 27.2, and HomePod 27.2.

extraction.body: Apple has started rolling out iOS 27.2, bringing two notable features to its first foldable, the iPhone Duo. The update adds Apple Pencil support and Edge Light, a handy feature that improves visibility during video calls in low-light conditions. The iPhone Duo now supports the Apple Pencil (USB-C) on both its inner and outer displays. However, support is limited to the USB-C model. The Apple Pencil Pro and other Pencil models are not compatible with the foldable at the moment. The addition makes the iPhone Duo more versatile, especially for users who want to use its large inner display for note-taking and productivity. Moreover, there's Edge Light now, a feature previously available on macOS. For those unaware, it illuminates the user's face by displaying light around the edges of the screen, helping them look clearer during video calls in dimly lit environments. Edge Light works with FaceTime and third-party apps such as Zoom, eliminating the need for a separate light source in many situations. It should also pair well with the iPhone Duo's foldable design, which allows users to prop up the phone for hands-free calls. Beyond these iPhone Duo-exclusive additions, iOS 27.2 introduces several other improvements for eligible Apple iPhones. For starters, Siri AI gets support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish, alongside better use of personal context and previous conversations on Apple Intelligence supported devices. The update also brings suggested actions to Messages, user profiles to Apple TV, a refreshed Podcasts layout and expanded Dual Capture support for group FaceTime calls. To install the update, head over to Settings -> General -> Software Update on your eligible iPhone.

extraction.body: Apple gives iPad mini its biggest update ever Featuring a stunning OLED display in an even thinner and lighter design, a huge leap in performance, faster wireless connectivity, and water and dust resistance CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today unveiled the all-new iPad mini , featuring a stunning OLED display in an even thinner and lighter design, a huge leap in performance with A20 Pro, and water and dust resistance. 1 The larger 8.5-inch OLED display, also available with a nano-texture option, delivers higher contrast and more than 2x higher peak brightness than the previous-generation iPad mini for a brilliant and immersive viewing experience. 2 A20 Pro supercharges AI with Neural Accelerators in each GPU core and Dual 16-core Neural Engine. iPad mini now has a 12MP Center Stage front camera on the landscape edge that’s perfect for video calls, an innovative Acoustic Display for an even better audio experience, faster wireless and cellular connectivity, and fast-charge support. 3 With its incredible set of advanced features, it’s the most capable and versatile iPad mini ever. The new iPad mini is powered by iPadOS 27 with the next generation of Apple Intelligence and Siri AI, which can draw on a user’s personal context to help them find what they need, answer questions on virtually any topic with broad world knowledge, and understand what’s on their screen. 4 The combination of powerful features and game-changing iPadOS 27 capabilities makes the new iPad mini a compelling value. Customers can pre-order it along with the new Smart Folio starting Wednesday, October 28, with availability beginning Friday, November 6. “iPad mini is beloved for its fantastic portability, performance, and display by a wide range of users, from creators and small business owners to doctors, field service workers, and gamers,” said Dave Pakula, Apple’s vice president of Hardware Engineering. “With a remarkably thinner and lighter design, a stunning new OLED display, the incredibly powerful A20 Pro, and water and dust resistance, the new iPad mini is a huge leap forward for users who love having the full iPad experience in the palm of their hand.” At 5.4 mm thin, the new iPad mini is more portable than ever, and is available in two gorgeous finishes: a new midnight and a beautiful starlight. Remarkably thinner and lighter than the previous generation, iPad mini is now even easier to carry, whether a user is reading, working on the go, or using it with one hand. The new iPad mini is powered by iPadOS 27 with the next generation of Apple Intelligence and Siri AI, which can draw on a user’s personal context to help them find what they need, answer questions on virtually any topic with broad world knowledge, and understand what’s on their screen. 4 The combination of powerful features and game-changing iPadOS 27 capabilities makes the new iPad mini a compelling value. Customers can pre-order it along with the new Smart Folio starting Wednesday, October 28, with availability beginning Friday, November 6.

It also features an IP67 rating to protect against water and dust — ideal for a range of use cases, such as working outside on a rainy day or reading by the pool. 1

Together, these display advancements extend the versatility of iPad mini across an even wider range of use cases.

It is built using Apple’s latest 2-nanometer process technology and a new package inspired by M-series chips. Powered by a 7-core GPU with Neural Accelerators in each GPU core, iPad mini delivers up to 4.5x faster AI performance than the previous generation — perfect for AI tasks ranging from running on-device models in creative apps to running local LLMs. 3 And with the latest graphics architecture, including dynamic caching and hardware-accelerated mesh shading and ray tracing, graphics performance jumps by up to 2.7x — great for gaming and 3D rendering. 3 A20 Pro also features up to a 6-core CPU for up to 60 percent faster multithreaded performance for everyday tasks like editing photos and working across apps. 3

The 512GB configuration features a powerful Dual 16-core Neural Engine, which offers double the processing power of the previous generation, accelerating tasks in apps like Draw Things and Detail. The new iPad mini features an innovative Acoustic Display for an even better audio experience when gaming, watching videos, or editing content. Specially designed woofers are paired through the display to produce punchier bass and more volume. In addition, custom tweeters are now hidden between the glass and aluminum enclosure for clearer highs. The Acoustic Display also features a sealed enclosure that helps iPad mini achieve its IP67 rating.

iPad mini now features N1, an Apple-designed wireless networking chip that enables Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread. 5 N1 brings better performance when connected to 5GHz Wi-Fi networks and improves the overall performance and reliability of features like AirDrop and AirPlay. 6

It is designed to be durable and repairable, and meets Apple’s high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry. As with all Apple products, its paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based 10 and designed to be recycled.

coreStoryFacts.text: Apple gives iPad mini its biggest update ever
Cellular models of the new iPad mini feature C2, Apple’s next-generation cellular modem system.
C2 enables up to 50 percent faster cellular data speeds compared to the previous generation of iPad mini, with even greater power efficiency.
6 And with iPadOS 27, moving between cellular and Wi-Fi networks is more seamless than ever, so users can stay connected on a FaceTime call even while they’re in transit.
Siri AI is an entirely new version of Siri, powered by Apple Intelligence, that is profoundly more personal, capable, and conversational.
A20 Pro delivers a giant leap in performance for iPad mini, significantly boosting graphics and AI-intensive tasks.
It is built using Apple’s latest 2-nanometer process technology and a new package inspired by M-series chips.

3 And with the latest graphics architecture, including dynamic caching and hardware-accelerated mesh shading and ray tracing, graphics performance jumps by up to 2.7x — great for gaming and 3D rendering.

It is made with 35 percent recycled content overall, 9 including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure and 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery. iPad mini is manufactured with 40 percent renewable energy, like wind and solar, across the supply chain.
As with all Apple products, its paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based 10 and designed to be recycled.
3 With its incredible set of advanced features, it’s the most capable and versatile iPad mini ever.

iPadOS 27 also delivers an expansive set of improvements that make iPad more responsive, reliable, and easy to use, along with updates to Liquid Glass, including a new slider in Settings that gives users the option to personalize it, adjusting it anywhere from ultraclear to fully tinted to match their preference.
Apple revolutionized personal technology with the introduction of the Macintosh in 1984.
Today, Apple leads the world in innovation with iPhone, iPad, Mac, AirPods, Apple Watch, and Apple Vision Pro.

Apple’s six software platforms — iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, visionOS, and tvOS — provide seamless experiences across all Apple devices and empower people with breakthrough services including the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Pay, iCloud, and Apple TV.
Apple’s more than 150,000 employees are dedicated to making the best products on earth and to leaving the world better than we found it.
iPad mini supports both Apple Pencil (USB-C) and Apple Pencil Pro, giving users two incredible options to bring their ideas to life.

Siri AI can draw on personal context understanding to help users find what they need in the moment across their personal messages, emails, photos, and more; use onscreen awareness to take action related to the content on a user’s screen; and answer questions about virtually any topic.
Additionally, Apple Intelligence makes apps smarter and more useful.
Users can improve a photo’s composition after it’s been taken using tools such as upgraded Clean Up, Spatial Reframing, and Extend.
And now the all-new Image Playground app offers photorealistic imagery.
In Safari, Notify Me helps users monitor web pages for changes, like product restocks or price drops, and stay on top of updates.
Apple Intelligence uses on-device processing and Private Cloud Compute to help protect users’ privacy.
The latest news and updates, direct from Apple.

sources.title: Microsoft offers to buy out a quarter of its workforce
passages: On Monday, Microsoft said it will offer voluntary buyouts to eligible employees in select parts of the company.
CNBC reports that the buyouts will be offered to roughly 60,000 employees , or about a quarter of its global workforce.
The company describes the offer as an opportunity for employees who may have already been considering career moves outside Microsoft.

While Microsoft did not give a direct reason for the buyout package, it comes as the company has spent the last several years managing costs amid investment in AI infrastructure and data-center buildout.
The effort is the second time Microsoft has run a voluntary workforce reduction in 2026.
In April, the company offered its first voluntary retirement package to 8,750 US employees.
Microsoft will extend the voluntary exit offer (VEO) to qualifying employees in the United States, India, Canada, and the United Kingdom.

The company’s employee rankings are internal, but according to the salary and career database Levels.fyi , levels 65–67 correspond to principal positions, and 68–70 are at the partner/distinguished level.
According to Chief People Officer Amy Coleman, eligible organizations were selected “based on each business’s priorities, customer commitments and workforce needs.”
While layoffs remain the most common way to reduce headcounts in the tech world, Microsoft may be following Google’s playbook.
As Business Insider reported, Alphabet offered employees voluntary exit packages in June and October 2025, and again in February 2026.
Now, eligible Microsoft employees may have to decide whether to take a deal now or keep their jobs and face the uncertainty of future company-wide layoffs.
In comments to GeekWire in July, Coleman said Microsoft was looking into making voluntary exits part of workforce management more regularly.
She described the current VEO as something that “builds on what we learned earlier this year through the Voluntary Retirement Program.”
According to Microsoft’s blog , employees eligible for the VEO will be contacted via email on Monday.
Microsoft will announce its latest earnings after market close later this week.

coreStoryFacts.text: On Monday, Microsoft said it will offer voluntary buyouts to eligible employees in select parts of the company.
CNBC reports that the buyouts will be offered to roughly 60,000 employees , or about a quarter of its global workforce.
The company describes the offer as an opportunity for employees who may have already been considering career moves outside Microsoft.

While Microsoft did not give a direct reason for the buyout package, it comes as the company has spent the last several years managing costs amid investment in AI infrastructure and data-center buildout.
The effort is the second time Microsoft has run a voluntary workforce reduction in 2026.
In April, the company offered its first voluntary retirement package to 8,750 US employees.
Microsoft will extend the voluntary exit offer (VEO) to qualifying employees in the United States, India, Canada, and the United Kingdom.

The company’s employee rankings are internal, but according to the salary and career database Levels.fyi , levels 65–67 correspond to principal positions, and 68–70 are at the partner/distinguished level.
According to Chief People Officer Amy Coleman, eligible organizations were selected “based on each business’s priorities, customer commitments and workforce needs.”
While layoffs remain the most common way to reduce headcounts in the tech world, Microsoft may be following Google’s playbook.
As Business Insider reported, Alphabet offered employees voluntary exit packages in June and October 2025, and again in February 2026.
Now, eligible Microsoft employees may have to decide whether to take a deal now or keep their jobs and face the uncertainty of future company-wide layoffs.
In comments to GeekWire in July, Coleman said Microsoft was looking into making voluntary exits part of workforce management more regularly.
She described the current VEO as something that “builds on what we learned earlier this year through the Voluntary Retirement Program.”
According to Microsoft’s blog , employees eligible for the VEO will be contacted via email on Monday.
Microsoft will announce its latest earnings after market close later this week.
Microsoft offered voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees, or about 27% of its global workforce, as the company spends heavily on artificial intelligence.

Amy Coleman wrote in a blog post that “The Voluntary Exit Offer is new for us,” and she said Microsoft would “keep helping people focus on the work that matters most, build new skills and, where it makes sense, find new opportunities across Microsoft.” Microsoft said the voluntary exit offer was available to eligible employees in Canada, India, the United Kingdom and the United States, and the company said employees must be at the vice president level or below to qualify.

Microsoft told Business Insider that eligible employees will have until early December to decide whether to take the offer and exit at the end of the year, and a Microsoft spokesperson said there are no plans for another buyout at this time.
Participants receive severance packages and career-planning resources.

Microsoft’s buyout offers are individualized based on an employee’s level, location, and tenure, and employees at internal levels 64 and below were offered one week of base pay per six months of service.
Microsoft’s capital expenditures for the September quarter should exceed $50 billion, and in the same quarter a year ago capital spending and finance leases came to $34.9 billion.
Microsoft is preparing a massive exodus of workers and inviting 60,000 people to leave in a gigantic voluntary departure.
Microsoft opens the door to voluntary departures to trim the workforce quietly: offering money to employees to leave the company on their own terms.

extraction.body: Bitcoin’s $BTC $84,459.46 rally has stalled in recent weeks, leaving prices listless around $80,000. In a market where sentiment shifts quickly, this has led some bears to warn of a renewed price crash. But Galaxy remains confident in bitcoin’s long-term prospects, saying it’s time to accumulate. “We think the bear market ended in June and that bitcoin is in the accumulation phase that has preceded every prior advance,” Alex Thorn, head of firmwide research at Galaxy, said in a note titled “Why now is the time to add and hold $BTC .” Galaxy Digital is a U.S. financial and infrastructure firm founded in 2018 by billionaire Mike Novogratz. It is headquartered in New York City and trades on Nasdaq under the ticker GLXY. According to Thorn, the bear market likely ended in June under $58,000, and improving price-chart signals, reduced selling pressure, and mounting fiscal risks make the largest cryptocurrency by market capitalization attractive to accumulate. He added that bitcoin has entered an accumulation phase resembling periods that preceded previous advances. Bitcoin traded around $80,000 at the time of the article, up 38% from June lows under $58,000. Still, prices are down approximately 35% from the record high of over $126,000. Returning to that high would require a gain of roughly 53%. Thorn highlighted bitcoin’s bullish recovery above its 50-week moving average after spending 44 weeks below it. Five consecutive weekly closes above that level have strengthened his conviction that the market had bottomed. Positioning also supports the thesis, Thorn argued. Asset managers’ net long exposure through CME bitcoin futures had fallen 57% from the week of the record high, while several major trading firms substantially reduced ETF holdings. That’s a sign that fast money has left, leaving the market in much healthier shape. “The fast money has left, the base stayed, and everything else is priced for perfection,” Thorn said. Other investors have been buying the dip. Galaxy said spot bitcoin ETFs added 87,000 $BTC following the June low, suggesting renewed directional demand as arbitrage activity declined. The firm sees rising U.S. debt, persistent deficits, and rising interest costs strengthening bitcoin’s appeal as a fixed-supply asset. Meanwhile, institutional enthusiasm for stablecoins and tokenization, alongside fading interest in bitcoin, resembles sentiment around previous market lows, according to Thorn.

extraction.body: Bitcoin’s $BTC $84,459.46 rally has stalled in recent weeks, leaving prices listless around $80,000. In a market where sentiment shifts quickly, this has led some bears to warn of a renewed price crash. But Galaxy remains confident in bitcoin’s long-term prospects, saying it’s time to accumulate. “We think the bear market ended in June and that bitcoin is in the accumulation phase that has preceded every prior advance,” Alex Thorn, head of firmwide research at Galaxy, said in a note titled “Why now is the time to add and hold $BTC .” Galaxy Digital is a U.S. financial and infrastructure firm founded in 2018 by billionaire Mike Novogratz. It is headquartered in New York City and trades on Nasdaq under the ticker GLXY. According to Thorn, the bear market likely ended in June under $58,000, and improving price-chart signals, reduced selling pressure, and mounting fiscal risks make the largest cryptocurrency by market capitalization attractive to accumulate. He added that bitcoin has entered an accumulation phase resembling periods that preceded previous advances. Bitcoin traded around $80,000 at the time of the article, up 38% from June lows under $58,000. Still, prices are down approximately 35% from the record high of over $126,000. Returning to that high would require a gain of roughly 53%. Thorn highlighted bitcoin’s bullish recovery above its 50-week moving average after spending 44 weeks below it. Five consecutive weekly closes above that level have strengthened his conviction that the market had bottomed. Positioning also supports the thesis, Thorn argued. Asset managers’ net long exposure through CME bitcoin futures had fallen 57% from the week of the record high, while several major trading firms substantially reduced ETF holdings. That’s a sign that fast money has left, leaving the market in much healthier shape. “The fast money has left, the base stayed, and everything else is priced for perfection,” Thorn said. Other investors have been buying the dip. Galaxy said spot bitcoin ETFs added 87,000 $BTC following the June low, suggesting renewed directional demand as arbitrage activity declined. The firm sees rising U.S. debt, persistent deficits, and rising interest costs strengthening bitcoin’s appeal as a fixed-supply asset. Meanwhile, institutional enthusiasm for stablecoins and tokenization, alongside fading interest in bitcoin, resembles sentiment around previous market lows, according to Thorn.

extraction.body: AVIEW Aorta Metrics enables automated aortic segmentation and diameter measurements across anatomical regions, broadening the quantitative capabilities of chest CT. Oct. 26, 2026 — Coreline Soft has received U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) 510(k) clearance for AVIEW Aorta Metrics, its AI-powered aortic quantitative analysis software. The clearance, received on Oct.16, brings the company's total to 13 FDA 510(k) clearances. AVIEW Aorta Metrics is a software medical device designed to automatically segment the aorta from chest CT images and provide quantitative diameter measurements across anatomical regions. The software automatically classifies aortic zones and measures the diameter of each zone, supporting consistent quantitative evaluation. It also provides straightened CPR (curved planar reformation), cross-sectional and 3D views, and analysis reports. The latest FDA clearance aligns with Coreline Soft's multi-disease analysis strategy based on chest CT imaging in the U.S. market. In the U.S. medical imaging AI market, there is growing demand for the ability to extract additional, clinically meaningful quantitative information from existing CT scans and to integrate these insights seamlessly into established Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS) and radiology interpretation workflows. As a result, interest is rising in Opportunistic screening, which leverages existing imaging data without requiring additional scans, as well as in quantitative imaging biomarkers. In response to these trends, Coreline Soft has developed its AVIEW platform to analyze multiple diseases and quantitative indicators from a single chest CT scan. AVIEW LCS and AVIEW Lung Nodule CAD support lung nodule detection and quantitative analysis for lung cancer screening and nodule management. AVIEW CAC automatically analyzes coronary artery calcium from non-contrast chest CT scans, delivering quantitative scoring and assessments for clinical interpretation. With the addition of AVIEW Aorta Metrics, Coreline Soft has further expanded its analytical capabilities in the U.S. market beyond pulmonary disease to encompass cardiovascular quantitative imaging, including CAC and aortic assessment. Coreline Soft's U.S. business is also evolving beyond individual hospital deployments toward deeper integration with clinical workflows and healthcare platforms. The company is advancing PACS-integrated, "zero-click" automation in collaboration with INFINITT North America (INA). Coreline Soft is also working with Optellum to explore the integration of AVIEW Lung Nodule CAD into a broader lung nodule management pathway, from detection and risk assessment to follow-up care. Separately, Coreline Soft has collaborated with Oatmeal Health on approaches related to lung cancer risk assessment and U.S. reimbursement pathways. The FDA clearance of AVIEW Aorta Metrics adds aortic quantitative analysis to Coreline Soft's U.S. chest CT portfolio and provides a regulatory foundation for expanding its quantitative imaging capabilities. extraction.body: Artificial intelligence-based software enables automated enhanced visualization of CT images of the lungs, heart and aorta September 26, 2019 — The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has cleared three modules of AI-Rad Companion Chest CT, an intelligent software assistant from Siemens Healthineers that brings artificial intelligence (AI) to computed tomography (CT) . They include the AI-Rad Companion Engine (K183272), Pulmonary (K183271) and Cardiovascular (K183268) modules. Representing the first intelligent assistant of the new AI-Rad Companion platform, AI-Rad Companion Chest CT helps radiologists interpret images of the thorax (chest) quickly with desired accuracy and precision, and automatically documents these findings as structured reports. Although CT chest images are mainly assessed by radiologists with regard to the primary indication, these images contain additional clinically relevant information. The algorithms in AI-Rad Companion Chest CT were trained on extensive datasets and annotated by qualified clinical specialists to provide segmentation, measurement and highlighting of key anatomical structures, to support quantitative and qualitative analysis. Using CT images of the chest, AI-Rad Companion Chest CT differentiates among various structures in that region – including the lungs, heart and aorta – highlights them individually, and marks and measures potential abnormalities, such as coronary calcifications. It supports a variety of tasks, including: Automated detection of lesions, localization of abnormalities and measurement of lung lesions ; Detection of nine anatomical landmarks as identified by American Heart Association (AHA) guidelines. Based on the AI-supported analysis, AI-Rad Companion Chest CT automatically generates standardized, reproducible, and quantitative reports in Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine (DICOM) SC format. In addition to reducing time spent on manual results documentation, these reports can be accessed by radiologists on the picture archiving and communication system (PACS) in the clinical routine. AI-Rad Companion Chest CT also highlights potentially clinically relevant changes that might otherwise remain unnoticed because they were not the primary indication for the exam. AI-Rad Companion Chest CT is a cloud-based solution that has been tested and validated for CT scanners from Siemens Healthineers, GE Healthcare and Philips Healthcare. It uses certified, secure teamplay infrastructure and integrates seamlessly into existing clinical workflows. extraction.body: Artificial intelligence-based software enables automated enhanced visualization of CT images of the lungs, heart and aorta September 26, 2019 — The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has cleared three modules of AI-Rad Companion Chest CT, an intelligent software assistant from Siemens Healthineers that brings artificial intelligence (AI) to computed tomography (CT) . They include the AI-Rad Companion Engine (K183272), Pulmonary (K183271) and Cardiovascular (K183268) modules. Representing the first intelligent assistant of the new AI-Rad Companion platform, AI-Rad Companion Chest CT helps radiologists interpret images of the thorax (chest) quickly with desired accuracy and precision, and automatically documents these findings as structured reports. Although CT chest images are mainly assessed by radiologists with regard to the primary indication, these images contain additional clinically relevant information. The algorithms in AI-Rad Companion Chest CT were trained on extensive datasets and annotated by qualified clinical specialists to provide segmentation, measurement and highlighting of key anatomical structures, to support quantitative and qualitative analysis. Using CT images of the chest, AI-Rad Companion Chest CT differentiates among various structures in that region – including the lungs, heart and aorta – highlights them individually, and marks and measures potential abnormalities, such as coronary calcifications. It supports a variety of tasks, including: Automated detection of lesions, localization of abnormalities and measurement of lung lesions ; Detection of nine anatomical landmarks as identified by American Heart Association (AHA) guidelines. Based on the AI-supported analysis, AI-Rad Companion Chest CT automatically generates standardized, reproducible, and quantitative reports in Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine (DICOM) SC format. In addition to reducing time spent on manual results documentation, these reports can be accessed by radiologists on the picture archiving and communication system (PACS) in the clinical routine. AI-Rad Companion Chest CT also highlights potentially clinically relevant changes that might otherwise remain unnoticed because they were not the primary indication for the exam. AI-Rad Companion Chest CT is a cloud-based solution that has been tested and validated for CT scanners from Siemens Healthineers, GE Healthcare and Philips Healthcare. It uses certified, secure teamplay infrastructure and integrates seamlessly into existing clinical workflows. extraction.body: UN Assistant Secretary-General, Assistant Administrator of the United Nations Development Program (UNDP) and UNDP Regional Director for Europe and the CIS Ivana Zivkovic made her first official visit to Turkmenistan. The purpose of the visit was to participate in the International Forum “Dialogue is a Guarantee of Peace”, as well as to hold high-level meetings to discuss issues of strategic partnership between UNDP and Turkmenistan. On December 11, the UNDP Regional Director met with the President of Turkmenistan Serdar Berdimuhamedov. During the conversation, potential areas of strategic partnership aimed at promoting inclusive and sustainable growth of the country were discussed. Taking part in the International Forum “Dialogue is a Guarantee of Peace”, Ivana Zivkovic addressed the forum participants. “UNDP remains a strategic partner of Turkmenistan in its quest for development, peace and stability. In the face of unprecedented global challenges, it is vital to use development as a key tool to achieve peace and stability. In this regard, I warmly welcome Turkmenistan’s initiatives to promote dialogue towards peace, mutual understanding and conflict resolution throughout the world,” she noted. During her stay in Turkmenistan, Ivana Zhivkovic also met with senior representatives of the Government of Turkmenistan, including Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Rashid Meredov, Deputy Prime Minister Nurmuhammed Amannepesov and Director General of the Agency for Transport and Communications under the Cabinet of Ministers of Turkmenistan Mammetkhan Chakyev. The parties discussed the country's development prospects and opportunities for expanding joint efforts to implement the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. The UNDP Regional Director highlighted the achievements of long-term cooperation between UNDP and the Government of Turkmenistan and discussed opportunities to further develop and strengthen this partnership in various areas, including democratic governance, health, digital transformation, education, environment and inclusive economic development. As part of her visit, the UNDP Regional Director visited the cardboard and printing workshop No. 1 of the Society of the Blind and Deaf of Turkmenistan (SBDT) in Ashgabat and took part in the celebration of the International Day of Neutrality. We previously reported that the Director of the UNDP Regional Bureau will visit Turkmenistan. extraction.body: UN Assistant Secretary-General, Assistant Administrator of the United Nations Development Program (UNDP) and UNDP Regional Director for Europe and the CIS Ivana Zivkovic made her first official visit to Turkmenistan. The purpose of the visit was to participate in the International Forum “Dialogue is a Guarantee of Peace”, as well as to hold high-level meetings to discuss issues of strategic partnership between UNDP and Turkmenistan. On December 11, the UNDP Regional Director met with the President of Turkmenistan Serdar Berdimuhamedov. During the conversation, potential areas of strategic partnership aimed at promoting inclusive and sustainable growth of the country were discussed. Taking part in the International Forum “Dialogue is a Guarantee of Peace”, Ivana Zivkovic addressed the forum participants. “UNDP remains a strategic partner of Turkmenistan in its quest for development, peace and stability. In the face of unprecedented global challenges, it is vital to use development as a key tool to achieve peace and stability. In this regard, I warmly welcome Turkmenistan’s initiatives to promote dialogue towards peace, mutual understanding and conflict resolution throughout the world,” she noted. During her stay in Turkmenistan, Ivana Zhivkovic also met with senior representatives of the Government of Turkmenistan, including Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Rashid Meredov, Deputy Prime Minister Nurmuhammed Amannepesov and Director General of the Agency for Transport and Communications under the Cabinet of Ministers of Turkmenistan Mammetkhan Chakyev. The parties discussed the country's development prospects and opportunities for expanding joint efforts to implement the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. The UNDP Regional Director highlighted the achievements of long-term cooperation between UNDP and the Government of Turkmenistan and discussed opportunities to further develop and strengthen this partnership in various areas, including democratic governance, health, digital transformation, education, environment and inclusive economic development. As part of her visit, the UNDP Regional Director visited the cardboard and printing workshop No. 1 of the Society of the Blind and Deaf of Turkmenistan (SBDT) in Ashgabat and took part in the celebration of the International Day of Neutrality. We previously reported that the Director of the UNDP Regional Bureau will visit Turkmenistan. passages: Now you can add Broadcom ( AVGO ) to the list.
According to Reuters, which obtained Anthropic's IPO prospectus , Broadcom is lending up to $42 billion to Anthropic for its infrastructure buildout.
Wall Street analysts and investors have raised concerns about circular investing at multiple points throughout the AI buildout.
Broadcom rivals Nvidia and AMD have also provided funding to their own customers, including OpenAI and Anthropic, which the labs then used to pay for access to the companies' high-powered chips.

In April, Anthropic announced it was teaming up with Broadcom and Google for a deal that would see Google provide its Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) capacity to Anthropic, with the supply coming online in 2027 .
Anthropic isn't just purchasing chips, though.
The company is also leaning on Broadcom for equipment leasing and financing, Reuters reports.
In turn, Anthropic is estimated to spend so much on Broadcom's technologies that the Claude developer will become the chip designer's largest compute customer by 2027.

extraction.body: An interesting new asset linked to Bitcoin ( BTC -0.29% ) might make its debut soon. On Oct. 19, BlackRock ( BLK +0.84% ) submitted filings to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) seeking permission to issue a new Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF), the iShares Bitcoin Managed Protection ETF, ticker PBIT. Unlike the asset manager's other Bitcoin ETF, the iShares Bitcoin Trust , the new one, if it's approved, is intended to soften Bitcoin's declines in exchange for capping its gains, according to the filing. But how would that work, and would it make the new ETF worth buying if the SEC gives BlackRock the go-ahead? Bitcoin is a great asset to own, but its main drawback, volatility, is more than many investors can stomach. In its lifetime so far, the coin has experienced numerous declines of about 80%. Even when its pullbacks and bear markets are shallower than that, they can still be quite painful; it's now 35% less than its all-time highs of $126,000, set about a year ago. To address this problem, BlackRock's new ETF would put a limit on those losses, like a seat belt that also puts a hard ceiling on the vehicle's top speed. Under the hood, the ETF would buy call options (rights to buy an asset at a set price, called the strike) on its main spot Bitcoin ETF, targeted at near 90% of its starting value. Then it would sell call options at higher strike prices to pay for the purchased calls. Each tranche's initial loss exposure is thus about 10% before fees, while the sold calls cap the gains above their strike price. Three overlapping tranches would be rolled monthly, so the downside insurance would be kept up to date at regular intervals, and each new tranche's cap would reset higher or lower according to market conditions. After a rally, each new tranche's buffer would start further below the current price. This idea isn't completely novel, and it has held up well in at least one recent test. One ETF issued by Calamos targets full downside protection rather than a 10% buffer, and it lost just 1% of its value during its one-year protection period starting October 2025, while Bitcoin entered a bear market and plunged. The catch is that the lost opportunity cost can be high during crypto bull markets, and even during regular seasonality. Another Calamos 10%-buffer fund had a 22.2% upside cap for its one-year outcome period beginning Feb. 2, 2026. Across Bitcoin's entire historical performance, it has grown by a median of 26.6% in the fourth quarter. For all of 2024, it gained 119.5%. That would be a lot of upside to miss out on. The new ETF's upside limits aren't disclosed yet. The Managed Protection ETF's fee hasn't been disclosed yet, either. BlackRock's spot Bitcoin ETF charges 0.25% per year. If that's anything to go by, the additional features included with the Managed Protection ETF mean that its expense fee will likely be higher. Calamos' 10%-buffer fund charges 0.69% per year. In contrast, holding Bitcoin directly on an exchange or in a crypto wallet incurs no annual fee, though exchanges do charge transaction fees for each purchase and sale. Taxes could be an issue, too. BlackRock's prospectus states that its options strategy backing the ETF could generate short-term gains, which would then be taxed as ordinary income, thereby further damping the after-tax returns versus owning the asset directly. So should you buy this new fund if the SEC says it can launch? Probably not, unless you're an investor who wants to own some Bitcoin but is fearful of panic-selling. Even then, a small position or regular purchases in modest amounts may be easier to live with. By capping upside, the fund trims the short, vigorous rallies that drive much of Bitcoin's return. And without that, there are better assets to own that don't cost as much in fees. Alex Carchidi has positions in Bitcoin and iShares Bitcoin Trust. extraction.body: An interesting new asset linked to Bitcoin ( BTC -0.29% ) might make its debut soon. On Oct. 19, BlackRock ( BLK +0.84% ) submitted filings to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) seeking permission to issue a new Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF), the iShares Bitcoin Managed Protection ETF, ticker PBIT. Unlike the asset manager's other Bitcoin ETF, the iShares Bitcoin Trust , the new one, if it's approved, is intended to soften Bitcoin's declines in exchange for capping its gains, according to the filing. But how would that work, and would it make the new ETF worth buying if the SEC gives BlackRock the go-ahead? Bitcoin is a great asset to own, but its main drawback, volatility, is more than many investors can stomach. In its lifetime so far, the coin has experienced numerous declines of about 80%. Even when its pullbacks and bear markets are shallower than that, they can still be quite painful; it's now 35% less than its all-time highs of $126,000, set about a year ago. To address this problem, BlackRock's new ETF would put a limit on those losses, like a seat belt that also puts a hard ceiling on the vehicle's top speed. Under the hood, the ETF would buy call options (rights to buy an asset at a set price, called the strike) on its main spot Bitcoin ETF, targeted at near 90% of its starting value. Then it would sell call options at higher strike prices to pay for the purchased calls. Each tranche's initial loss exposure is thus about 10% before fees, while the sold calls cap the gains above their strike price. Three overlapping tranches would be rolled monthly, so the downside insurance would be kept up to date at regular intervals, and each new tranche's cap would reset higher or lower according to market conditions. After a rally, each new tranche's buffer would start further below the current price. This idea isn't completely novel, and it has held up well in at least one recent test. One ETF issued by Calamos targets full downside protection rather than a 10% buffer, and it lost just 1% of its value during its one-year protection period starting October 2025, while Bitcoin entered a bear market and plunged. The catch is that the lost opportunity cost can be high during crypto bull markets, and even during regular seasonality. Another Calamos 10%-buffer fund had a 22.2% upside cap for its one-year outcome period beginning Feb. 2, 2026. Across Bitcoin's entire historical performance, it has grown by a median of 26.6% in the fourth quarter. For all of 2024, it gained 119.5%. That would be a lot of upside to miss out on. The new ETF's upside limits aren't disclosed yet. The Managed Protection ETF's fee hasn't been disclosed yet, either. BlackRock's spot Bitcoin ETF charges 0.25% per year. If that's anything to go by, the additional features included with the Managed Protection ETF mean that its expense fee will likely be higher. Calamos' 10%-buffer fund charges 0.69% per year. In contrast, holding Bitcoin directly on an exchange or in a crypto wallet incurs no annual fee, though exchanges do charge transaction fees for each purchase and sale. Taxes could be an issue, too. BlackRock's prospectus states that its options strategy backing the ETF could generate short-term gains, which would then be taxed as ordinary income, thereby further damping the after-tax returns versus owning the asset directly. So should you buy this new fund if the SEC says it can launch? Probably not, unless you're an investor who wants to own some Bitcoin but is fearful of panic-selling. Even then, a small position or regular purchases in modest amounts may be easier to live with. By capping upside, the fund trims the short, vigorous rallies that drive much of Bitcoin's return. And without that, there are better assets to own that don't cost as much in fees. Alex Carchidi has positions in Bitcoin and iShares Bitcoin Trust. It expects the crypto to return 10% annually during that period, versus 7.5% for U.S. large-cap stocks, 5.6% for broad U.S. bonds, and 5.5% for gold.
Although the figures it calculated are unlikely to prove true in 2036, the drivers for those results are hard to argue against, and it's my view that JPMorgan Chase is directionally correct.
Overall, JPMorgan Chase's projections for Bitcoin's price growth are on the bearish side compared to Bitcoin's history, but they look reasonable.
The coin has a 10-year compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 63%.
